goal: 100 source-disjoint candidates for reviewable Upstream work; no automatic fork or publication grant
selection_rule: Baseline existing verified forks; prepared historical AWAITING_EXTERNAL packets without a fork and current MIT/Apache-2.0 license; fill with unbatched S1=A/S2=C Index assessments having explicit interference, coordination and limitation evidence, current MIT/Apache-2.0 metadata and activity since 2026-09-01. Screening precedence uses mechanism specificity, code references and assessment recency; not stars.

prepared_packets_missing_forks.finding: Inspect first-party Python scientific evidence policy, linting and provenance schema boundaries for deterministic unsupported-payload admission using fixed in-memory data and native tests only; do not run scientific tasks, ADK agents, model critics or API providers.

The assessed S2=C constructor detects cross-run file overlap and routes affected plan commitments into an approval-gated adjustment. Test whether current first-party overlap analysis misclassifies create/delete or path alias changes and whether the unchanged plan is preserved when adjustment is withheld, using native deterministic fixtures only.

Inspect first-party Python browser trajectory checkpoint and critical-resume input validation using fixed data structures only. No Playwright browser launch, live desktop interaction, Fara model agent, benchmark rollout, or hosted inference is permitted.

The assessed S2=C witness is an exclusive task/worker claim and completed-prerequisite gate. Check whether every native claim entry point, including direct manual API dispatch, enforces exactly one active task per agent and only admits ready tasks; use first-party engine functions with fixed in-memory state, no running agents.

Index S2=C describes shared-owner atomic token reservations and settlement across concurrent goal runs. Prospectively test failure/retry at reservation-to-settlement boundaries: a released or retried claim must not strand budget or double-credit an owner while another run proceeds.

Assessment credits first-party file-intersection checks that serialize overlapping builder waves and a single integrator. Inspect current source file-scope collision classification and admission for a falsifiable safe native change; do not invoke actual builder agents, model calls or dry-run agent episodes.

The assessed S2=C witness serializes and verifies shared session-memory updates. Screen current first-party memory.py plus test_memory_concurrency.py for a falsifiable lost-update or stale-write failure between separate sessions, with isolated files and no agent or provider invocation.

AgentFlow ships first-party declarative task-graph specs, ready-node selection, persisted status and result-schema logic. Screen deterministic Python validation and dependency/retry bookkeeping using fixed local data, excluding model CLI invocations or mocked model task runs.

agentUniverse owns Python agent templates, workflow metadata and configured state/step transitions. Screen exact first-party non-model schema and admission functions through offline script cases, not its ReAct inference loop, multi-agent framework execution or model evaluations.

OniRoute ships first-party Python workspace governance, quality and validation modules around engineering artifacts. Screen deterministic validator and path-boundary handling on pinned real source using fixed local fixtures, not its model-backed engineering runner or simulated swarm-wave subsystem.

CubeLoop's first-party Python checkpoint/session, HITL and deferred-work components preserve execution state; use fixed-input native tests to screen saved-state consistency and approval gates without running any model-backed session.
Raven-Code has a first-party read-before-edit/stale-content ledger; screen whether any current native failure remains despite the existing guard.

Screen local Python per-domain experience-library persistence, validation and context-tree transformations with filesystem and fixed-data script inputs, not its proposer, executor, demo agent, benchmark, task rollouts or model selection.

Screen first-party Node WORKBOARD claim admission and deterministic dispatch metadata for conflicts, stale claims or unsafe path parsing using synthetic fixed input files only. Do not invoke Copilot review, any subagent, GitHub writes or a model host.

Cyber AI Team has first-party owner authorization and action-policy decisions around business-domain work. Screen pure Python policy validators and transition guards with fixed inputs only; exclude ERPNext, PostgreSQL, Temporal company cycles, LLM agents, simulated model plans or any external business actions.
The installed plugin includes first-party Python bootstrap and adoption validators; screen input validation and idempotency with native Python scripts only, without calling a host LLM skill.

Inspect the Python operator-mcp workflow graph validator with finite in-memory workflow specifications for incorrect DAG or step-argument admission. Limit validation to source-native no-provider Python and no shell execution, running workflows, supervisor agents or MCP side effects.

OpenOrbit ships Electron/TypeScript first-party mutation approvals and agent-reply guards around its personal-assistant loop. Check deterministic permission and malformed-event boundaries via native script tests, without launching Electron, providers or agents.
MAREF Python code-evolution and local guardrail routines produce code and test outcomes; inspect fixed-input state/error propagation with native Python tests, not model-generated candidates.

ConnectOnion has a first-party Python tool executor and optional approval plugin. Screen native approval, request validation and tool admission helpers with deterministic inputs only; no packaged co ai instance, LLM replies, subagent task or shell/browser side effect.

Reins provides first-party Python capability registry and invocation policy guards ahead of the model-facing operation loop; inspect native script tests on deny/allow, audit metadata and argument boundaries without invoking a provider.

Evidence Loom ships Python numeric/research-readiness and frozen-evidence validators used with its bundled analyst workflow; screen deterministic malformed-input/provenance checks from real source without market API, model, or Tauri invocation.

Active Graph has a first-party Python event log, typed graph patches and optimistic conflict checks. Screen script-only event-patch validation and replay invariants using genuine modules and fixed input events; do not invoke recorded, mocked or live LLM-backed goal behaviors.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Concurrent writable subagents operating on the same tree can race, explicitly identified in the agent tool's concurrency contract.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Readonly agents share safe batches; readOnly:false agents run in an exclusive awaited batch, with readonly modes physically excluding edit/write/bash.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Background writable delegates are outside this mutual-exclusion guarantee; no cross-process/global shared-file reservation or complete semantic merge protocol is claimed.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Duplicate task submissions or competing sandbox/device admissions and reused application state when attempts overlap or a runner resumes.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Unique task/attempt claims and task-scoped leases, bounded concurrency, backpressure gating and selected retry/reconcile rules.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: The batch is optional; an individual local run has no distinct S2 peer set. Deterministic conflict avoidance cannot be upgraded to S2=A without autonomous coordination discretion.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous integrations or mutable resource claims create conflicting ownership and duplicate/stale actions.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `reservations.execute(action=acquire)` checks active holder, normalized resource and scope, denies different live claimant unless holder actually ceased; lease alone never steals live claim.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: reservation metadata does not itself sandbox files, and overlap query is advisory for declared paths; credit is restricted to exclusive *resource* ownership arbitration.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: concurrent updates to a lesson from stale snapshots, resurrecting a retired lesson, incompatible parallel advice replacing a newer record and duplicated overlapping recommendations.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: each specialist returns keep/adapt/retire/defer for frozen lesson IDs; host requires expected revisions and atomic publication, rejects conflicting writes, reloads the latest lesson snapshot, then re-invokes model reconciliation rather than accepting last-writer-wins. Same-scope overlap is consolidated; unrelated scopes cannot rewrite each other.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: conflict witness is shared retained lessons across runs, not all inter-agent workflow interference. Worker/reviewer fanout and graph scheduling alone are not used as S2 proof.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: duplicate claim/overwrite or a stale worker publishing a checkpoint after another acquired the issue.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: unique fenced owner and CAS replacement rule, with cancellation/refusal on lease loss.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: this is a narrow collision-attenuation path, not proof of a broad adaptive peer-negotiation metasystem.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: competing top-level `runner` and `goal` ownership of one Git worktree can cause Git checkout/commit interference. `workspace-lock.ts` explicitly identifies this conflict.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `wireProject` instantiates one shared `WorkspaceLock`; the runner acquires it as owner `runner`, goal mode holds it as `goal`, a competing owner receives `busy`, and nested goal-owned code runner uses reentrant `goal` ownership.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: lock is in-process and does not prove cross-process or distributed exclusion. Alternative top-level execution modes may be seen as exclusive rather than co-active S1s; this is the principal semantic boundary to review before canonical admission.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: parallel children share the same filesystem, and write-capable tools could overwrite or race on a path or a process-mutated workspace.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: a process-global `ResourceLockManager` arbitrates conflicting declared file/workspace claims and delays incompatible requests before executing effects.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: locks do not persist across detached processes, hold across entire multi-step subagent workflows, prevent logical stale-read/write errors after the lock releases, or make parallel `arena` file edits safe. Those limits preclude a general S2=A claim.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous children can read one file, form edits on the same original bytes, then overwrite one another; the first-party commentary records this and a real concurrent-replace regression test.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: a static per-canonical-path lock spans the entire read-modify-write and stale-content validation; `WriteIfUnchangedAsync` refuses obsolete edits.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: per-file safety is narrower than negotiated scheduling over whole-repository edits. Across distinct processes the in-process lock does not apply; stale-content check remains a separate guard.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous hook claims to a shared channel continuation token are structurally mutually exclusive; without arbitration, messages accepted by the losing candidate would be lost or processed by a duplicate cell.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: session startup attempts hook ownership; a conflict makes the losing candidate dispose and stop, while the settlement step forwards its already accepted `send` command into the existing owner's inbox.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: no broader cross-team semantic coordination is credited; most workflow batch scheduling and subagent fan-out alone are not S2.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: finite global child execution slots are contended for by distinct active/queued child agents; descendant waits can deadlock a parent occupying its own needed slot, and one pool's queue can starve another.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: per-pool FIFO with round-robin across pools, and explicit wait-yield plus priority slot reacquisition for dependent parents.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: the positive S2 witness is bounded to local child-agent contention. Shared blackboard, DAG dependencies and concurrent child count alone are not independent positive witnesses. No autonomous S2 arbitration is asserted.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: redundant simultaneously running alternatives consuming capacity, stale handoffs and sibling actions on incompatible intermediate results.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: the coordinator may select the first useful race result and cancel other running siblings; configured send/check message and explicit dependency handoff give sibling work a shared decision route instead of independent conflicting continuation.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: race and dependency patterns are optional compositions, not a proved default arbitration loop for all peers.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous attempts to act on the same project task and downstream work using unfinished or reassigned output risk duplicate/conflicting execution.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: atomic start reservation, nonterminal duplicate-start rejection, assignment revalidation and completed-dependency requirement.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: this does not prove general conflict avoidance for agents editing the same external file or that every project elects this mode.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: overlapping file/subtree modification and shared-provider quota contention.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: declared-scope conflict detector plus reservations and concurrency cap.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: undeclared write scopes are not locked; worktree-isolated absolute paths do not conflict; queue enforcement is not an autonomy claim.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: a foreground turn can conflict with an in-flight background iteration over the same installation's mutable execution/workspace context.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: foreground arrival preempts/refuses background execution at effect boundaries under one shared lock/signalling relation.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Bounded source assessment of the supported distribution; no live model or performance claim.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: two clients could claim/edit the same assignment or stale work could commit over a newer candidate/champion state.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: exclusive client/identity-bound candidate leases, candidate-scoped file access and round locks/compare-and-swap champion commits.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: C records function-specific first-party coordination support; not a claim of autonomous conflict negotiation or measured parallel scalability.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: two workers or successive assignments targeting one mutable task can contend for a single task owner, causing duplicate task-state writes/commitments.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: TeamCoordinator invokes atomic TaskStore.claim before worker process startup; claim rejects a task owned by another worker and a bound worker cannot update a different task.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: This is static source evidence, not a live benchmark; scope is limited to first-party packaged operation.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Concurrent worker attempts to claim/edit shared queue/board state and overlapping assignment acquisition.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Exclusive file lock during queue pop/report publish with one active_task per worker, plus synchronized manager phase/report board.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Read-only specialists also limit file-write interference; no native general semantic conflict/oscillation resolution is demonstrated.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous edits to the same or inferred-overlapping repository paths can create collision/conflict and invalidate assumptions between independently acting workers.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Bernstein withholds a candidate batch when `owned_files`, inferred paths, lock-manager ownership or active worktree diffs overlap, while isolated worktrees and serialized merge paths keep admitted work separated until landing.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: dependency ordering, task claiming, shared whiteboard and ordinary message transport are not independently credited as S2. The positive witness is specifically the live overlap/isolation feedback path.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: overlapping parallel write scopes, conflicting edits on the same file/contract, stale shared checkout state and duplicate incompatible ownership claims.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Runtime requires declared exact files/write roots or coordination contracts, checks active overlaps before mutation, or launches truly isolated worktrees. Workflow validation rejects parallel writable tasks with intersecting scopes, while manager/worker receipts permit later non-conflicting merge/handoff.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: applies to declared write-resource collisions, not automatic model-led balancing of all competing worker goals.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: concurrent makers can target one repository and create overlapping/stale/incompatible changes or merge conflicts that disturb other makers' operations.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: worktree isolation plus rail-governed merge, retry/replant, conflict handling and state refresh coordinate those competing operations.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: generic ContextEngine scheduling or parallelism is not the witness. The positive witness is the rail path specifically addressing concurrent maker write/integration interference.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: calls from different sessions can contend for the same provider credential and named-pool capacity. The router explicitly shares credential pools across named pools so multiple consumers cannot each spend the full limit of one key.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: shared pre-call lease/reservation, pool/credential concurrency/rate/token/spend limits, route selection/failover and post-call reconciliation serialize/account for the scarce capacity.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: one-shot `/v1/fanout` children are not the positive witness. The S2 witness is the deployment's multiple durable autonomous chat sessions sharing one quota-bearing router.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Two members can try to claim the same card or re-create a task, or act on shared files with unfinished earlier edits.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: BoardStore atomic claim/status gate, stable issue-key deduplication, dependency/ready checks and one project RunGuard lock.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: No fine-grained path leases, parallel worktree model agents, global conflict negotiation or dynamic model ownership of the lock rule.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: competing peers could both treat the same pending task as theirs; child and parent attempts could race while a predecessor is unresolved, causing duplicate work or invalid integration.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: atomic claim checks current task state and Preset compatibility, rejects a second claimant; staged children only become runnable after a successful source Run, while parent waits until all children finish; failed children block the parent.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: this is narrow coordination of task ownership/dependencies, not general negotiation of conflicting goals, cost allocation, global fairness or distributed consensus.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous heavy execution on different cache keys exhausts host resources; duplicate task claimants risk inconsistent writes.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: one machine-wide admission queue/budget and trusted task-lease family prevent uncontrolled concurrency at the contested resources.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: task claim family may legitimately reuse a lease; no S2 agent that plans optimal resource allocation is claimed. The machine-wide ledger spans local operations but is not evidence of cross-project organizational S3.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Multiple workers can race for the same ready item or act on stale revision/ownership
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Claim/release with exact revision and owner, observe expiry, then reload/reconsider after conflict
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: This is specific claim-contention regulation, not generic DAG/messaging. Host-issued namespace grant and coordinating actor/policy must be composed. Advisory resource claims do not globally enforce exclusivity.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: unbounded sibling token consumption would deplete the parent quota needed for other children and the parent convergence step.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: delegate_many invokes allocateChildBudgets, divides the available budget into child quotas and reserves a separate coordination share, then passes enforceable ceilings to individual child loops.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: the budget mechanism is inactive when no parent token budget is configured; children are read-only and thus do not create a qualifying shared-file write conflict. No generalized coordination beyond bounded token contention is claimed.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Concurrent spawned workers share a Git checkout by default and can race/overwrite one another's edits or create merge conflicts; first-party worktree service explicitly identifies these exact hazards ([src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/worktree_service.py](https://github.com/awslabs/cli-agent-orchestrator/blob/ffa9fc742c7d47ce038d3d951ccc5527ba0c0218/src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/worktree_service.py#L1-L10)).
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Supervisor's opt-in worktree parameter causes CAO to create distinct branch/checkouts for individual child sessions, separating conflicting write contexts; worker results return to the supervisor for explicit integration.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Positive restricted to explicitly enabled per-worker worktree mode; default shared directory does **not** receive this S2 closure. No automatic conflict-free merge or code acceptance is claimed.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: concurrent child tools would otherwise overlap shared permission prompts, first-party Git checkpoints, auto-test execution and shared worktree file mutations. Those effects can collide or be observed at unstable partial states.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `Agent.executeDelegatedTool` wraps each delegated action under one parent-owned `delegatedMu` and routes it through the same permission/mode/checkpoint executor; `ParallelAgents` runs model loops concurrently while delegated concrete tool effects are mutually exclusive.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: no per-child Git worktree, transaction-level mutual exclusion, changed-file reconciliation or guaranteed prevention of sequential lost updates. The coordination claim is restricted to synchronized delegated tool executions and shared helper state.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous heavy command invocation against the same finite Mac build/simulator resource.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: atomic priority-ordered lease claim and worker-side shim mediation.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: shims cover declared command patterns, not every subprocess or arbitrary heavy command; a worker bypassing PATH or invoking an unclassified tool need not be protected.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: opposite actions `open_protected_circuit` and `close_protected_circuit` share a resource key, while equal desired outcomes could execute twice.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `ResourceGate` arbitrates holders by resource identity, outcome, scope and current state; `DispatchCoordinator` attempts Tier D before other work.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: the S1 cells are independently event-triggered skill operations sharing an inference substrate, not separate permanently running LLM processes; S2 credit is bounded to their actuator conflict, not arbitrary inter-agent messaging.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: concurrent peer jobs contend for one target agent, and distinct returned work results race on the source conversation/checkpoint; native tests specifically exercise target serialization and per-thread followups.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: _process serializes target invocation by target_agent_id and synthesis by source_thread_id/source_agent_id, with a concurrency envelope.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: async delivery requires a host TeamProcessor; synchronous generic ask_agent alone is not the S2 witness.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: overlap of nonterminal writers' declared `expected_write_scope` paths, checked against current sibling task records rather than conjectured from generic messaging.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: registry computes a specific write-scope conflict and returns `scope_conflict`, `suggested_task_id` and `serialize_or_worktree` advice to the delegating agent; targeted `notify` and `cancel` are first-party response controls.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: scopes are declarations, not confinement; two writers still launch on an overlap, and model-mediated correction was not dynamically exercised. If the constructor threshold requires a fully installed autonomous response rather than a first-party function-specific response interface, the S2 grade should be revisited rather than silently promoted to `A`.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Concurrent modifications or git/PR operations can contend over common repository integration state.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Worktree separation, per-repository locks and explicit CI/conflict-aware PR integration rules.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: This is a bounded source-first inspection of one frozen supported first-party mode, not a production reliability claim or credit for unshipped external providers.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: multiple mutating children writing in the same inherited git checkout risk overwriting or contaminating one another's file changes; concurrent children also compete for bounded active/parallel slots.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: before fan-out, `spawn_parallel` rejects more than one mutating inherited sibling unless `allow_shared_mutation` is deliberately selected; `delegate` establishes mandatory isolated worktree lease for mutating branch-mode child and fails closed if required isolation cannot be created.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: no claim that S2 is autonomously negotiated, always enabled, or proven effective by independent benchmark. Counterexample `allow_shared_mutation: true` opts out of the attenuation.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: two leaders modifying the same file can clobber one another; a reader and writer of the same path can produce a torn or inconsistent observation.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `scheduleWorkItems` normalizes paths and partitions model-declared work into topological layers and waves with no writer/writer or reader/writer file overlap; unscoped mutations run alone; dispatch waits for prior waves and blocks dependents when predecessors fail.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: leader-generated file lists can be incomplete or dishonest, and ad-hoc parallel `run_leader` calls are not guaranteed to pass through this file-overlap wave scheduler.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Duplicate seat/task acquisition, lost task-store updates and mixed edits/index operations.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Check-and-launch under one lock, serialize writes by canonical store identity, honor claims and isolate worktrees.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Store-lock coverage and OS enforcement are limited to the documented wrappers/launch surfaces, not every possible third-party writer.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: two worker S1s can claim/write an overlapping source file in the same checkout, observe an out-of-date version of another worker's changed file, or contribute overlapping changes that would overwrite diverged main checkout content when merging isolated worktrees.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `FileClaimRegistry` refuses double ownership, logs/reports stale reads and actively emits `FileConflict`; preclaims reject inconsistent `paths` before work; default separate worktrees quarantine writes and three-way guarded merge declines conflicting paths rather than silently clobbering main.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: same-checkout conflicts are observed only through claimed file operations; undeclared semantic conflicts and independent manually launched sessions are not guaranteed covered. Worktree conflicts can remain for manual/follow-on resolution.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: overlapping current instructions and contest over destination session attention/execution while it is already busy.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: explicit per-worker exclusive command admission/denial and returned busy state, distinct from simple status reporting or generic queue.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: this regulates competing instructions to one session, not all simultaneous file writes or a complete team workflow protocol.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: Simultaneous provider calls from a large fan-out cause shared service throttling (`429` bursts), degrading each child's progress; source explicitly calls out this concrete failure mode.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Configured MaxConcurrentSubAgents creates a channel-semaphore admission gate shared across child runs within the respective delegation tool; waiting children pause instead of starting simultaneous provider use.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: An unconfigured (zero) cap is unlimited; positive C is explicitly bounded to deployments setting a finite cap. It does not prevent semantic write conflicts between children.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: concurrent turns can request the same output path, both observe it as free and silently overwrite one another's work if probe and write are not coordinated.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `uniquifyPathForWrite` serializes path decision plus write on a mutex keyed by the requested path; after the first write, the losing writer sees the collision and receives a suffixed path rather than overwriting the winner.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: shell-side writes can bypass `write_file` conflict protection, so the S2 claim is bounded to the first-party coordinated write-tool path rather than every possible filesystem mutation.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: A builder's code or contract can overlap another builder's changed files, produce a Git conflict, or invalidate a frozen test already passed by another task.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: Planned file ownership/dependencies, serialized merge lock, affected-tests integration gate and explicit capped rebasing of collided tasks.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: Mere DAG edges would not establish S2 without the identified collision-response/return path.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: simultaneous jobs can contend for limited worker slots/capabilities and create duplicate or unaccounted external work after lost leases.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: the central lease ledger and resource/capacity matching prevent overlapping claims and account for stale completions.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: resource allocation is deterministic and no autonomous S2 arbiter is credited.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: independent predecessor branches resolve concurrently and might start the same downstream worker more than once; duplicate active task runs might overwrite or intermingle their task-specific shared conversation.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: graph incoming-edge resolution waits for all predecessor decisions, aggregates accepted outputs, and atomically claims each target using `DashSet::insert`; concurrent workflow's task-level `DashSet` denies duplicate in-flight same-key runs, released when the run exits.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: no global scheduling or shared-resource arbitration across unrelated swarm instances; graph joins and task guards do not prove resource-level coordination for arbitrary side effects.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: overlapping edits, correction/review artifacts and uncertain ownership when both remediation workers target the same repository state.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: one privileged remediation lane per worktree plus queue/resource admission; a second worker is refused until ownership is resolved.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: `max_concurrency` alone would only be generic resource limiting; the worktree-specific duplicate remediation refusal is the material positive witness. No conflict-free deployment was empirically tested.

new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_interference: two agents can edit a shared document from different revisions, overwrite the same binary/non-OT file, or issue competing candidate changes against a protected shared path.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.observed_coordination: `submit_operation` transforms revision-aware text edits against intervening operations; `write_file` enforces `expected_revision` and creates a frozen conflict on a stale divergent write; task intents/participant slices surface collisions.
new_index_hypothesis_screens.reported_limitation: the reviewer separation for project conflicts is human/member-based, distinct from the in-session model Reviewer and not an automatic S3* claim.
